The [blue whale](/wiki/Blue_whale "Blue whale") is the heaviest living animal.

The heaviest living animals are all [whales](/wiki/Whale "Whale"). There are considerable obstacles to overcome in obtaining accurate weights for them, however, as no scale can accommodate the whole body of a large whale. Whaling factories are usually enlisted to help accomplish the task, but it still remains difficult, and most weighings have been done by parts of flensed whales, leaving much room for error. Mathematical formulas have also been devised to estimate the average weight of various whale species based on body length, but this method is equally prone to inaccuracy.[[22]](#cite_note-22)

Seven of the nine colonial colleges began their histories as institutions of higher learning. The other two developed out of existing preparatory schools. The [University of Pennsylvania](/wiki/University_of_Pennsylvania "University of Pennsylvania"), an [Ivy League](/wiki/Ivy_League "Ivy League") university in [Philadelphia](/wiki/Philadelphia "Philadelphia"), began operating in 1751 as the [Academy of Philadelphia](/wiki/Academy_of_Philadelphia "Academy of Philadelphia"), a secondary school founded by [Benjamin Franklin](/wiki/Benjamin_Franklin "Benjamin Franklin"), and later added an institution of higher education in 1755 following the granting of a charter to the [College of Philadelphia](/wiki/College_of_Philadelphia "College of Philadelphia"). [Dartmouth College](/wiki/Dartmouth_College "Dartmouth College"), an Ivy League college in [Hanover, New Hampshire](/wiki/Hanover,_New_Hampshire "Hanover, New Hampshire"), began operating in 1768 as the collegiate department of [Moor's Charity School](/wiki/Moor%27s_Charity_School "Moor's Charity School"), a secondary school founded in 1754 by [Eleazar Wheelock](/wiki/Eleazar_Wheelock "Eleazar Wheelock"), the college's founder. Dartmouth considers its founding date to be 1769, when it was granted a collegiate charter.
